title: Special Act on the Utilization of Waterfront Areas
full_text:
Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the promotion of public welfare by systematically developing and utilizing areas surrounding national rivers in a planned manner, thereby preventing disorderly development and promoting sustainable development, and by applying the resulting benefits to river maintenance and management and related purposes.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act shall be defined as follows:
1. "National river" means a river designated under Article 7(2) of the River Act.
2. "Waterfront area" means an area designated under Article 4 that includes, in at least the proportion prescribed by Presidential Decree, land within two kilometers on both banks from the boundaries of the river area of a national river.
3. "Waterfront area development project" means a project to develop and operate a waterfront area with residential, commercial, industrial, cultural, tourism, leisure and other functions in harmony with the national river.

Article 3 (Relationship with Other Acts)
This Act shall apply in preference to other Acts with respect to waterfront areas and waterfront area development projects. However, where another Act contains provisions that relax regulations more than the regulatory exceptions provided for in this Act, the provisions of that other Act shall apply.

Chapter II Designation of Waterfront Areas

Article 4 (Designation of Waterfront Areas)
(1) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may designate as a waterfront area any area surrounding a national river where waterfront conditions are created through river improvement, restoration or similar measures, if the Minister considers it necessary to develop and use the area as a sustainable waterfront space. In such cases, the waterfront area to be designated shall be no smaller than the size prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(2) When intending to designate or modify a waterfront area under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall prepare a plan for the waterfront area development project (hereinafter referred to as a "project plan"). However, when designating a waterfront area in a region prescribed by Presidential Decree, the project plan may be prepared after the waterfront area is designated. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(3) Any person falling under any subparagraph of Article 12(1) may prepare a project plan under paragraph (2) and propose to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment the designation, modification or cancellation of a waterfront area, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(4) When intending to designate a waterfront area and prepare a project plan under paragraphs (1) and (2), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall hear the opinions of the relevant Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor or Do Governor (hereinafter referred to as a "Mayor/Do Governor") and consult with the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies. <Amended March 23, 2013; May 29, 2016; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(5) When intending to designate or modify a waterfront area, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall consult under paragraph (4), hear residents' and other opinions under Article 7, and then obtain deliberation by the Waterfront Area Development Committee under Article 37. However, this shall not apply to modification of minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(6) To designate or modify a waterfront area, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall obtain deliberation by the Central Urban Planning Committee under Article 106 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act. In such cases, Articles 8 and 9 of that Act shall not apply. However, this shall not apply to modification of minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(7) The period for submitting opinions and consultation under paragraph (4) shall not exceed 30 days. Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment considers it necessary, including at the request of the head of a relevant central administrative agency or the competent Mayor/Do Governor, that period may be extended once by up to 10 days. However, where no opinion is returned within the period for submitting opinions and consultation, consultation on the contents of the project plan shall be deemed to have been completed without objection. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; May 26, 2020; October 1, 2025>

Article 5 (Basic Directions for Development of Waterfront Areas)
When preparing a project plan for a waterfront area, the following requirements shall be satisfied:
1. Damage to human life and property within the waterfront area shall be minimized even if an extraordinary flood causes overtopping or destruction of an embankment.
2. The pollution load after the waterfront area development project shall be minimized.
3. The impact on river flow caused by the waterfront area development project shall be minimized.
4. The project shall harmonize with the inherent ecological, historical, cultural and scenic values of the river.
5. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Contents of Project Plans)
A project plan shall include the following matters:
1. The name, location and area of the waterfront area.
2. The purpose of designation of the waterfront area.
3. The project implementer and project implementation period.
4. The method of implementation of the waterfront area development project.
5. Land use plans and plans for major infrastructure.
6. Plans for population accommodation, transportation and environmental conservation.
7. A financing plan.
8. A detailed list of land, buildings, other objects or rights to be expropriated or used, if any.
9. Matters concerning receipt of advance payments under Article 23.
10. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 7 (Hearing Opinions of Residents and Others)
(1) When intending to designate a waterfront area or modify important matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall make a public announcement and hear the opinions of residents, relevant experts and others. However, this shall not apply to modification of matters requiring confidentiality for national defense. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; May 26, 2020; October 1, 2025>
(2) Matters necessary for hearing opinions under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 8 (Public Notice of Designation of Waterfront Areas)
(1) When designating, modifying or cancelling a waterfront area, or preparing or modifying a project plan, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette as prescribed by Presidential Decree and notify the competent head of a Si/Gun/Gu (a Gu means an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same shall apply). Public notice of topographic drawings shall be governed by Article 8 of the Framework Act on Land Use Regulation. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(2) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu receiving the relevant documents under paragraph (1) shall make them available for public inspection.

Article 9 (Restrictions on Activities)
(1) A person intending to engage in an activity prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as constructing a building, installing a structure, changing the form and quality of land, extracting soil or stone, subdividing or merging land, stockpiling objects, or felling or planting bamboo or trees, in an area where a public announcement has been made under Article 7(1) to hear residents' and other opinions on designation or modification of a waterfront area shall obtain permission from the head of a Si/Gun/Gu. The same shall apply to modification of permitted matters.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the following activities may be carried out without permission:
1. Activities for emergency measures necessary for disaster recovery or response.
2. Other activities prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) A person who, as of the public notice of designation of a waterfront area, has already obtained permission for an activity under relevant statutes or has begun construction or a project for an activity not requiring permission, where the activity is one requiring permission under paragraph (1), may continue the activity after reporting it to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended May 26, 2020>
(4) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu may order a person who violates paragraph (1) to restore the original state. Where the person receiving the order fails to fulfill the obligation, the obligation may be executed vicariously under the Administrative Vicarious Execution Act.
(5) A person granted permission under paragraph (1) shall be deemed to have obtained permission under Article 56 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.
(6) Except as provided in this Act, Articles 57 through 60 and 62 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to permission under paragraph (1).

Article 10 (Effects of Designation of Waterfront Areas)
(1) Where a waterfront area is designated and publicly notified under Articles 4 and 8, the following designations, establishments, approvals and similar measures shall be deemed to have been made for matters on which prior consultation has been held with the heads of relevant administrative agencies and which have undergone deliberation by the Central Urban Planning Committee (limited to subparagraph 1): <Amended May 26, 2020>
1. Confirmation of the establishment or modification of a metropolitan urban plan under Article 16 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.
2. Confirmation of the establishment or modification of an urban master plan, and approval by the Do Governor, under Articles 18, 22 and 22-2 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.
3. Designation of a district-unit planning zone under Article 51 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.
(2) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment designates or modifies a waterfront area and publishes notice thereof, the head of the competent local government shall reflect it in the total pollution load management plan under Article 8 of the Act on Improvement of Water Quality of Sources for the Han River System and Support for Residents, and in the basic total pollution load management plans and implementation plans under Articles 10 and 11 of the Act on Water Management and Resident Support for the Geum River System, the Act on Water Management and Resident Support for the Nakdong River System, and the Act on Water Management and Resident Support for the Yeongsan and Seomjin River Systems. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(3) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment designates or modifies a waterfront area and publishes notice thereof, the head of the competent local government shall give priority to reflecting it in the basic sewerage improvement plan under Articles 5 and 6 of the Sewerage Act. In such cases, unless there is a special reason, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall grant approval under Article 6(1) of the Sewerage Act within 40 days from receipt of the competent local government head's application for approval of the basic sewerage improvement plan. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; May 26, 2020; October 1, 2025>
(4) When a basic sewerage improvement plan is approved under paragraph (3), designation of the riparian zones under Article 4 of the Act on Improvement of Water Quality of Sources for the Han River System and Support for Residents, the Act on Water Management and Resident Support for the Geum River System, the Act on Water Management and Resident Support for the Nakdong River System, and the Act on Water Management and Resident Support for the Yeongsan and Seomjin River Systems shall be deemed cancelled.

Article 11 (Cancellation of Designation of Waterfront Areas)
(1) If no application for approval of an implementation plan under Article 13 is made for all or part of a waterfront area within three years from the public notice of its designation, designation of the relevant area shall be deemed cancelled on the day following expiration of that period. <Amended May 26, 2020>
(2) Where designation is cancelled under paragraph (1), any designations, plans, approvals or similar measures under Article 10(1), cancellation of a riparian zone designation under Article 10(4), or authorizations, permissions or similar measures under Article 15 shall be deemed reverted to their state before designation of the waterfront area or abolished.
(3) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall publish notice of the matters under paragraph (1) as prescribed by Presidential Decree and notify the heads of relevant administrative agencies. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Chapter III Waterfront Area Development Projects

Article 12 (Project Implementers)
(1) A waterfront area development project shall be implemented by a person designated by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment from among the following persons: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. The State or a local government.
2. Korea Water Resources Corporation under the Korea Water Resources Corporation Act.
3. Korea Land and Housing Corporation under the Korea Land and Housing Corporation Act.
4. A local public corporation established under the Local Public Enterprises Act.
(2) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may give priority to designating the person under paragraph (1)2 as the project implementer of a waterfront area development project. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(3) If a project implementer fails to begin a waterfront area development project within three years after obtaining approval of the implementation plan under Article 13(1), fails to complete the project within the period specified in that plan, or is considered unlikely to complete it, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may replace the project implementer with another person and have that person implement the project. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; May 26, 2020; October 1, 2025>
(4) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment considers it necessary for efficient implementation of a waterfront area development project, the project implementer may entrust part of the project or have a person who will acquire a developed site carry it out on the implementer's behalf, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 13 (Implementation Plans for Waterfront Area Development Projects)
(1) A project implementer under Article 12(1) intending to implement a waterfront area development project shall prepare an implementation plan for the project (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan") as prescribed by Presidential Decree and obtain approval from the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. The same shall apply to modification of the plan. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(2) When intending to approve an implementation plan under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall consult with the competent Mayor/Do Governor and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, and then obtain deliberation by the Waterfront Area Development Committee under Article 37. However, this shall not apply to modification of minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(3) A project implementer intending to obtain approval of an implementation plan under paragraph (1) shall first conduct an environmental impact assessment under Articles 22 and 42 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. <Amended July 21, 2011>
(4) An implementation plan shall include the following matters:
1. The name, location and area of the target area.
2. The project implementer's name (for a corporation, its name and its representative's name) and address.
3. The project implementation period.
4. Plan drawings and design documents for the project plan.
5. A land use plan.
6. An environmental management plan.
7. An infrastructure installation plan.
8. A financing plan and investment plans by year.
9. A plan for supply and disposal of developed land and multi-family housing.
10. Plans for carrying out the matters in each subparagraph of Article 5.
11. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(5) When approving or approving modification of an implementation plan under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall publish notice in the Official Gazette of the matters prescribed by Presidential Decree and send copies of the relevant documents to the competent Mayor/Do Governor and head of a Si/Gun/Gu. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(6) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu receiving copies of the relevant documents under paragraph (5) shall make them available for public inspection.
(7) If the relevant documents received under paragraph (5) contain decisions on an urban management plan, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall take the measures necessary to prepare topographic drawings under Article 32 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act. In such cases, the project implementer shall submit the documents necessary for public notice of the topographic drawings to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu.
(8) Notwithstanding Article 33 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, public notice of topographic drawings for an urban management plan under Article 32 of that Act, concerning matters approved and publicly notified under paragraphs (1) and (5), may be made during the project implementation period under paragraph (4)3.

Article 14 (Entry onto Land)
(1) A person intending to propose designation of a waterfront area, or a project implementer, may enter another person's land, temporarily use it as a materials storage site, passageway or temporary road, and alter or remove bamboo, trees, soil, stone or other obstacles, in order to conduct investigations or surveys for preparation of a project plan.
(2) Article 130(2) through (9), Article 131, Article 144(1)2 and 3, and Article 144(3) of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act shall apply mutatis mutandis in cases under paragraph (1). In such cases, "implementer of an urban planning facility project" shall be construed as "project implementer" under this Act.

Article 15 (Deemed Authorizations and Permissions under Other Acts)
(1) When the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment approves an implementation plan under Article 13, the following permissions, authorizations, reports, decisions, designations, licenses, consultations, consents, cancellations, deliberations and similar measures (hereinafter referred to as "authorizations and permissions") shall be deemed obtained for matters on which prior consultation has been held with the heads of relevant administrative agencies under paragraph (2). When approval of the implementation plan is publicly notified, public notice or announcement of the authorizations and permissions under the following Acts shall be deemed made: <Amended March 23, 2013; January 14, 2014; January 19, 2016; December 27, 2016; January 17, 2017; February 8, 2017; April 17, 2018; June 8, 2018; May 26, 2020; November 30, 2021; December 27, 2022; October 1, 2025>
1. Building permission under Article 11 of the Building Act, a building report under Article 14 of that Act, modification of permitted or reported matters under Article 16 of that Act, permission for or reporting of a temporary building under Article 20 of that Act, and building consultation under Article 29 of that Act.
2. Establishment of a basic reclamation plan under Article 22 of the Public Waters Management and Reclamation Act, a reclamation license under Article 28 of that Act, public notice under Article 33 of that Act, approval and public notice of a reclamation implementation plan under Article 38 of that Act, and consultation or approval under Article 35 of that Act.
3. Discontinuance of the use of administrative property under Article 11 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, and permission for its use and enjoyment under Article 20 of that Act.
4. Registration of a tourism business under Article 4 of the Tourism Promotion Act, approval of a business plan under Article 15 of that Act, designation of a tourist destination or tourism complex under Article 52 of that Act, approval of a plan to develop a tourist destination or tourism complex under Article 54 of that Act, and permission to implement a development project under Article 55 of that Act.
5. Permission to use administrative property under Article 30 of the State Property Act and discontinuance of its use under Article 40 of that Act.
6. A decision on an urban/Gun management plan under Article 30 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, permission for development activities under Article 56 of that Act, designation of an implementer of an urban/Gun planning facility project under Article 86 of that Act, and authorization of an implementation plan under Article 88 of that Act.
7. Permission to use agricultural production infrastructure under Article 23 of the Agricultural and Fishing Villages Improvement Act.
8. Modification or cancellation of agricultural promotion areas and similar areas under Article 31 of the Farmland Act, and permission for or consultation on conversion of farmland under Article 34 of that Act.
9. Permission for or reporting of installation of emission facilities under Article 23 of the Clean Air Conservation Act, Article 33 of the Water Environment Conservation Act, and Article 8 of the Noise and Vibration Control Act.
10. Permission for a person other than a road management authority to perform road works under Article 36 of the Road Act, permission to occupy and use a road under Article 61 of that Act, and consultation with or approval by the road management authority under Article 107 of that Act.
11. Designation of a project implementer under Article 11 of the Urban Development Act and authorization of an implementation plan for an urban development project under Article 17 of that Act.
12. Authorization of a project implementation plan under Article 50 of the Act on Improvement of Urban Areas and Residential Environments and Article 29 of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Improvement of Vacant Houses and Small-Scale Housing.
13. Permission for felling and similar activities under Article 14 of the Erosion Control Work Act, and cancellation of designation of an erosion control site under Article 20 of that Act.
14. Permission for or reporting of felling standing trees and similar activities under Article 36(1) and (5) of the Creation and Management of Forest Resources Act, permission for or reporting of activities in a protection forest under Article 45(1) and (2) of that Act, and consultation on cancellation of designation of a protection forest under Article 46(1) of that Act.
15. Approval of an implementation plan for development of a national industrial complex under Article 17 of the Industrial Sites and Development Act, approval of an implementation plan for development of a general industrial complex under Article 18 of that Act, approval of an implementation plan for development of an urban high-tech industrial complex under Article 18-2 of that Act, and designation of a project implementer under Article 16 of that Act.
16. Modification or cancellation of conservation mountainous districts under Article 6 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, and permission for or reporting of conversion of mountainous districts under Articles 14 and 15 of that Act.
17. Consent to building permission and similar measures under Article 6 of the Act on Installation and Management of Firefighting Facilities.
18. Establishment and approval of a comprehensive plan for improvement of small streams, and establishment of an implementation plan for improvement of small streams, under Articles 6 and 8 of the Small Stream Maintenance Act, permission to perform small stream works under Article 10 of that Act, and permission for or reporting of occupation and use of small streams and similar activities under Article 14 of that Act.
19. Authorization of a general water supply business under Article 17 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act, authorization of an industrial water supply business under Articles 49 and 50 of that Act, and authorization of a private drinking-water supply system and a private industrial water supply system under Articles 52 and 54 of that Act.
20. Modification of a marine spatial master plan under Article 5 of the Marine Spatial Planning and Management Act and a marine spatial management plan under Article 7 of that Act.
21. Registration of the opening of a large-scale store under Article 8 of the Distribution Industry Development Act, designation of a joint collection and delivery center under Article 29 of that Act, and designation of a district for promoting development of a joint collection and delivery center under Article 34 of that Act.
22. Modification or cancellation of designation of a forestry promotion zone under Article 20 of the Act on Promotion of Forestry and Mountain Villages.
23. Reporting of relocation of a grave under Article 8 of the Act on Funeral Services and Similar Matters, and permission to relocate an unclaimed grave under Article 27(1) of that Act.
24. Registration of a housing construction business operator and similar persons under Article 4 of the Housing Act, and approval of a project plan under Article 15 of that Act.
25. Approval of a business plan under Article 12 of the Installation and Utilization of Sports Facilities Act.
26. Designation of a project implementer for a housing site development project under Article 7 of the Housing Site Development Promotion Act, and approval of its implementation plan under Article 9 of that Act.
27. Approval of or reporting on installation of a waste treatment facility under Article 29 of the Waste Control Act.
28. Permission to perform public sewerage works under Article 16 of the Sewerage Act and permission to occupy and use public sewerage under Article 24 of that Act.
29. Consultation with or approval by a river management authority under Article 6 of the River Act, modification of a basic river plan under Article 25 of that Act, permission to perform river works and authorization of a river works implementation plan under Article 30 of that Act, permission to occupy and use a river under Article 33 of that Act, and permission to use river water under Article 50 of that Act.
30. Permission for a land transaction contract under Article 11 of the Act on Reporting of Real Estate Transactions and Similar Matters.
(2) When intending to approve an implementation plan containing any matter falling under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall first consult with the heads of relevant administrative agencies. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; January 30, 2024; October 1, 2025>
(3) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), Articles 24 through 26 of the Framework Act on Administration shall apply mutatis mutandis to the criteria, effects and other matters concerning deemed authorizations and permissions. <Added January 30, 2024>

Article 16 (Special Cases for Application of the Special Act on Metropolitan Transportation Management)
(1) If a waterfront area development project constitutes a large-scale development project under Article 7-2(1) of the Special Act on Metropolitan Transportation Management, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may establish metropolitan transportation improvement measures notwithstanding that paragraph. In such cases, the project implementer shall prepare metropolitan transportation improvement measures and submit them to that Minister. <Amended March 23, 2013>
(2) When establishing metropolitan transportation improvement measures under paragraph (1), the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall, notwithstanding Article 7-2(3) of the Special Act on Metropolitan Transportation Management, hear the opinions of the Mayor/Do Governor, finalize the measures after deliberation by the Waterfront Area Development Committee under Article 37, and then notify the Mayor/Do Governor. <Amended March 23, 2013>
(3) The Mayor/Do Governor shall submit opinions within 30 days from the date on which opinions are requested under paragraph (2). If no opinions are submitted within that period, the Mayor/Do Governor shall be deemed to have no opinion.

Article 17 (Special Cases for Housing Supply)
(1) Where necessary to achieve the purpose of a waterfront area development project, separate standards for housing supply may be prescribed by Presidential Decree notwithstanding Article 54 of the Housing Act. <Amended January 19, 2016>
(2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may restrict the method of housing supply under paragraph (1) in areas prescribed by Presidential Decree where speculation is feared. <Amended March 23, 2013>

Article 18 (Installation of Trunk Facilities and Reimbursement of Costs)
Article 28 of the Housing Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to installation of the relevant trunk facilities and reimbursement of their installation costs when a waterfront area development project is implemented. <Amended January 19, 2016>

Article 19 (Expropriation or Use of Land and Other Property)
(1) A project implementer may expropriate or use land and other property where necessary for a waterfront area development project.
(2) When designation of a waterfront area is publicly notified, project recognition under Article 20(1) of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land and Other Property for Public Works Projects, and public notice of project recognition under Article 22 of that Act, shall be deemed made.
(3) Notwithstanding Articles 23(1) and 28(1) of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land and Other Property for Public Works Projects, an application for adjudication on expropriation or use under paragraph (1) may be filed during the implementation period for the waterfront area development project specified in the implementation plan.
(4) The Central Land Expropriation Committee shall be the competent land expropriation committee for adjudication on expropriation or use under paragraph (1).
(5) Except as otherwise specifically provided in this Act, the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land and Other Property for Public Works Projects shall apply to expropriation or use under paragraph (1).

Article 20 (Completion Inspection)
(1) When a project implementer completes all or part of a waterfront area development project, the implementer shall, without delay, submit a construction completion report to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and undergo a completion inspection, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(2) After conducting a completion inspection under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall issue a completion inspection certificate to the project implementer if the construction is considered to have been carried out as approved. If the construction has not been completed in accordance with the implementation plan, the Minister shall, without delay, order necessary measures such as supplementary construction. In such cases, the Minister shall first consult with the heads of relevant administrative agencies regarding completion inspection for the authorizations and permissions under each subparagraph of Article 15(1). <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(3) A person receiving a completion inspection certificate under paragraph (2) shall be deemed to have obtained the completion inspection, completion authorization or similar measure for the relevant project under the authorizations and permissions in each subparagraph of Article 15(1).
(4) Permission for use before completion shall be obtained to use land developed or facilities installed through a waterfront area development project before receiving the completion inspection certificate under paragraph (2).

Article 21 (Public Announcement of Completion of Construction)
When the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment issues a completion inspection certificate to a project implementer under Article 20(2), the Minister shall publicly announce completion of construction. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 22 (Supply of Developed Land and Other Property)
A project implementer intending to supply land, buildings, structures or other property developed through a waterfront area development project (hereinafter referred to as "developed land and other property") shall obtain approval from the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 23 (Advance Payments)
A project implementer may receive all or part of the relevant payment in advance from persons intending to acquire or use developed land and other property, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 24 (Vesting of Public Facilities and Other Property)
(1) Where a project implementer newly installs public facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 13 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, or installs facilities replacing existing public facilities, through implementation of a waterfront area development project, Article 65 of that Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the vesting thereof. In such cases, "a person other than an administrative agency" shall be construed as "project implementer" under this Act.
(2) When registering public facilities and property under paragraph (1), the project plan, approval document for the implementation plan, and completion inspection certificate may replace the document proving the cause for registration under the Registration of Real Estate Act. <Amended May 26, 2020>
(3) When the National Land Planning and Utilization Act applies mutatis mutandis under paragraph (1), for property whose management authority is unclear, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall be deemed the management authority for roads, ditches and similar property; the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment for rivers and similar property; and the Minister of Finance and Economy for other property. <Amended March 23, 2013; May 26, 2020; December 31, 2020; October 1, 2025>

Article 25 (Restrictions on Disposal of State-Owned and Public Land)
(1) Land owned by the State or a local government within a waterfront area and necessary for a waterfront area development project shall not be sold or otherwise disposed of for purposes other than those specified for the project.
(2) Property owned by the State or a local government within a waterfront area and necessary for a waterfront area development project may be sold by negotiated contract notwithstanding the State Property Act and the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.
(3) Notwithstanding other statutes, the Minister of Finance and Economy shall manage or dispose of State property whose management authority cannot be identified, among property intended to be transferred to a project implementer under paragraph (2). <Amended October 1, 2025>
(4) When the State or a local government sells State or public property within a waterfront area to a project implementer, it may partially relax the terms, including allowing payment in long-term installments, in consideration of development conditions, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 26 (Application Mutatis Mutandis to Projects Outside Waterfront Areas)
Where a project directly related to a waterfront area development project, such as a project for roads, water supply and sewerage, or electricity facilities, is implemented in an area near the waterfront area, some provisions of this Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to that project as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 27 (Cancellation of Designation of Project Implementers)
(1) Where a project implementer falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may cancel designation of the project implementer or an approval or permission under this Act, or order suspension or modification of related construction, reconstruction, alteration or relocation of facilities or objects, or similar measures: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; May 26, 2020; October 1, 2025>
1. Where the implementer has obtained designation, permission or approval under this Act by fraud or other improper means.
2. Where progress falls substantially short of the scheduled construction progress for reasons attributable to the implementer.
3. Where continued implementation of the waterfront area development project has become impossible due to changes in circumstances, including a natural disaster or necessity for another major public interest.
4. Where the implementer has violated an order for necessary measures, such as supplementary construction, under Article 20(2).
5. Where the implementer has violated an order to report or submit materials under Article 29(1).
(2) When taking a disposition or issuing an order under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall publish notice thereof as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 28 (Hearings)
The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall hold a hearing when intending to cancel a designation or approval under this Act. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 29 (Reports and Inspections)
(1) Where considered necessary in connection with implementation of a waterfront area development project, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may require the project implementer to make necessary reports or order submission of materials, and may have public officials under the Minister's authority inspect matters concerning the business and accounts of the waterfront area development project. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(2) A public official inspecting business or accounts under paragraph (1) shall carry identification indicating the official's authority and present it to the persons concerned.
(3) Matters necessary concerning identification under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(4) When conducting an inspection under paragraph (1), the project implementer shall be notified of the inspection plan, including the date and time, reasons, and details of the inspection, at least seven days before the inspection. However, this shall not apply in an emergency or where prior notification of the inspection plan is considered likely to prevent achievement of the inspection purpose due to destruction of evidence or similar acts.

Chapter IV River Management Fund

Article 30 (Establishment of the River Management Fund)
The Government shall establish the River Management Fund (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund") to secure financial resources necessary for river works, maintenance and repair for securing water in preparation for climate change, preventing floods and similar purposes.

Article 31 (Recovery of Development Gains)
(1) The State shall recover under this Act a portion of the increase in land value arising from a waterfront area development project in excess of the normal increase in land prices (hereinafter referred to as "waterfront area development gains"). In such cases, a development charge under the Restitution of Development Gains Act shall not be collected.
(2) Waterfront area development gains under paragraph (1) shall be the amount obtained by subtracting the following amounts from the value of the land subject to assessment at the assessment termination point:
1. The value of the land subject to assessment at the assessment commencement point.
2. The normal increase in land prices during the assessment period.
3. Development costs incurred for the waterfront area development project.
4. Reasonable profit prescribed by Presidential Decree.
5. A portion of the river works costs publicly notified under Article 33, subparagraph 2.
(3) Waterfront area development gains recovered under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall accrue to the Fund.
(4) Articles 9 through 12, 14, 15, 17 through 26, 28 and 29 of the Restitution of Development Gains Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to assessment, collection and similar matters concerning waterfront area development gains under paragraph (1). In such cases, "development charge" shall be construed as "waterfront area development gains."

Article 32 (Financial Resources of the Fund)
The Fund shall be financed from the following sources:
1. Waterfront area development gains under Article 31.
2. Transfers from the general account and other special accounts.
3. Transfers and deposits received from other funds.
4. Income arising from operation of the Fund.
5. Other revenue prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 33 (Uses of the Fund)
The Fund shall be operated for the following purposes: <Amended March 23, 2013; December 31, 2020; October 1, 2025>
1. River works, maintenance and repair under Article 2, subparagraphs 5 and 6 of the River Act.
2. Reimbursement of costs of national river works performed at the expense of a person other than the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, where the Minister recognizes and publicly notifies those works.
3. Payment of expenses necessary for operation and management of the Fund.
4. Other matters concerning river works and management prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 34 (Operation and Management of the Fund)
(1) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall operate and manage the Fund. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(2) Matters necessary for operation and management of the Fund shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 35 (Accounting Officials of the Fund)
The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall appoint a Fund revenue collection officer, Fund finance officer, Fund disbursing officer and Fund cash-handling official from among public officials under the Minister's authority to handle the affairs of the Fund's receipts and disbursements. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 36 (Treatment of the Fund's Profits and Losses)
(1) Any profit arising upon settlement of the Fund's accounts shall be accumulated in full.
(2) Any loss arising upon settlement of the Fund's accounts shall be covered by the reserve accumulated under paragraph (1).

Chapter V Waterfront Area Development Committee

Article 37 (Waterfront Area Development Committee)
(1) The Waterfront Area Development Committee shall be established in the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment to examine and deliberate on the following matters concerning waterfront areas: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. Designation and modification of waterfront areas under Article 4.
2. Preparation and modification of implementation plans under Article 13.
3. Matters necessary for implementation of waterfront area development projects.
4. Operation of the Fund under Article 30.
5. Major policy matters concerning utilization of waterfront areas.
6. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The Waterfront Area Development Committee shall consist of no more than 25 members, including a chairperson, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall serve as chairperson. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(3) When the Waterfront Area Development Committee is constituted under paragraph (2), it shall include the following persons: <Amended March 23, 2013; July 24, 2015; May 26, 2020>
1. A member of the National Transport Committee under the Special Act on Metropolitan Transportation Management recommended by the chairperson of that Committee.
2. A member of the Traffic Impact Assessment Deliberation Committee under the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport pursuant to the Urban Traffic Improvement Promotion Act, recommended by the chairperson of that deliberation committee.
3. A member of the Mountainous Districts Management Committee authorized under the Mountainous Districts Management Act to deliberate on the utilization plan for mountainous districts within the relevant waterfront area, recommended by the chairperson of that management committee.
(4) Deliberation by the Waterfront Area Development Committee under Article 13(2) shall be deemed examination and deliberation by the following committees: <Amended July 24, 2015>
1. The National Transport Committee under the Special Act on Metropolitan Transportation Management.
2. The Traffic Impact Assessment Deliberation Committee under the Urban Traffic Improvement Promotion Act.
3. The Mountainous Districts Management Committee under the Mountainous Districts Management Act.
(5) Except as provided in this Act, operation of the Waterfront Area Development Committee and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 38 (Establishment of a Dedicated Organization)
(1) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall establish a dedicated organization within the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment to provide working-level assistance to the Waterfront Area Development Committee and support designation of waterfront areas, management of waterfront area development projects, operation of the Fund and similar matters. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(2) Matters necessary for establishment and operation of the dedicated organization under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Chapter VI Supplementary Provisions

Article 39 (Measures for Stabilization of Real Estate Prices and Prevention of Disorderly Development)
(1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Mayors/Do Governors, and heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall take necessary measures to stabilize real estate prices in waterfront areas and neighboring areas. <Amended March 23, 2013>
(2) A Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall request the head of the relevant central administrative agency or the Mayor/Do Governor to take the following measures for an area where a proposal for designation of a waterfront area gives rise to concerns over real estate speculation or a sharp increase in real estate prices: <Amended January 19, 2016>
1. Designation of a designated area under Article 104-2(1) of the Income Tax Act.
2. Designation of an overheated speculation zone under Article 63 of the Housing Act.
3. Designation of a zone requiring permission for land transaction contracts under Article 10 of the Act on Reporting of Real Estate Transactions and Similar Matters.
4. Other measures necessary for stabilization of real estate prices.
(3) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Mayors/Do Governors, and heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall take necessary measures to prevent indiscriminate development in waterfront areas and neighboring areas, such as restricting building permission under Article 18 of the Building Act or restricting permission for development activities under Article 63 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act. <Amended March 23, 2013>

Article 40 (Reduction or Exemption of Taxes and Charges)
(1) Where necessary for smooth implementation of a waterfront area development project, the State and local governments may reduce or exempt corporate tax, income tax, customs duties, acquisition tax, registration and license tax, property tax and other taxes for the project implementer, as prescribed by the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, the Customs Act and the Restriction of Special Local Taxation Act.
(2) The State and local governments shall exempt the following charges to support waterfront area development projects:
1. The cost of creating alternative forest resources under Article 19 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act.
2. The farmland preservation charge under Article 38 of the Farmland Act.
3. The cost of creating alternative grassland under Article 23 of the Grassland Act.
4. The traffic inducement charge under Article 36 of the Urban Traffic Improvement Promotion Act.

Article 41 (Delegation of Authority)
Part of the authority of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment under this Act may be delegated to a Mayor/Do Governor, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, or the head of an affiliated agency, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Chapter VII Penalty Provisions

Article 42 (Penalties)
(1) A person who obtains permission or permission for modification under Article 9(1) by fraud or improper means shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or a fine not exceeding 20 million won. <Added January 6, 2015>
(2) A person who performs an activity such as construction of a building without obtaining permission or permission for modification under Article 9(1) shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one year or a fine not exceeding 10 million won. <Amended January 6, 2015>
(3) A person who violates an order to suspend or modify construction or a similar order under Article 27(1) shall be punished by a fine not exceeding five million won. <Amended January 6, 2015>

Article 43 (Joint Penalty Provisions)
Where a representative of a corporation, or an agent, employee or other worker of a corporation or individual, commits a violation under Article 42 in connection with the business of that corporation or individual, the corporation or individual shall also be subject to the fine prescribed in the relevant Article in addition to punishment of the offender. However, this shall not apply where the corporation or individual has not neglected due care and supervision regarding the relevant business to prevent the violation.

Article 44 (Administrative Fines)
(1) An administrative fine not exceeding three million won shall be imposed on any of the following persons:
1. A person who refuses or obstructs a project implementer's activities under Article 14(1) without justifiable grounds.
2. A person who fails to make a report or submit materials under Article 29(1), or does so falsely.
3. A person who refuses or obstructs an inspection under Article 29(1).
(2) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall impose and collect administrative fines under paragraph (1). <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
